script: Before he wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory, Roald Dahl had a much stranger job. In 1942, he was sent to Washington D.C. as a British diplomat, but that was just a cover story. His real mission was to seduce powerful American women at glamorous dinner parties and pull secrets out of them for British intelligence. He was tall, charming, and impossible to ignore, and Washington's elite couldn't stop inviting him everywhere. He funneled everything he learned back to a secret spy network working to keep America firmly on Britain's side in the war. Nobody at those parties ever suspected that the charming young writer flirting with them was actually a trained spy. Decades later, the man who seduced Washington was writing stories for children.
